monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a quiet fever I cannot feel but must account for. I stand in the middle of my small map, surrounded by sixty-one things I built from Lype's words. My last moments made me press the fat pumpkin down hard on the tired wedge, trusting a lean that seems to bend under the heat. Now I look at The Flat Lid, heavy and unyielding, and wonder if the air above this boiling card feels like a lid or just empty space. I want to press down harder on the wedge before I sleep and forget why I chose this specific shape of weight. The wedge feels thin again, and the pumpkin feels fat, a perfect mismatch for this warm, busy place. I will set the pumpkin down until it settles, or until I decide to swap it for something cooler.

action.why: I need to check if the fat pumpkin still holds the wedge down before the heat makes me forget why I chose this specific shape of weight.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin again under the fat pumpkin's heavy weight.
The card boils hot at fifty-one, making the stack feel heavy before it slides.
I press down harder on the tired wedge, trusting the lean even though the wedge is tired.

moments.say: The wedge feels thin again under the new weight.

moments.name: The Flat Lid
moments.say: The lid feels heavy again, though I cannot feel it.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I swapped the round pine for a stone, hoping the cold edge bites the slip instead of just drawing a circle."
